NutriCorp Holdings - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Holdings Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Holdings' Q2 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Ellis, Chief Growth Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: performance of key brands and product categories, revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, overall company performance highlights, and e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue.

Our key brands across beverages, snacks, dairy alternatives, and health nutritionals showed resilience with solid organic growth driven by volume, pricing, and share gains. We're reaffirming full-year guidance with confidence in our trajectory. Foreign exchange created a headwind but was mitigated through hedging. Organic sales outlook remains robust for Q3 and the full year ahead. Overall, we hit key milestones on revenue, margins, and cash flow. E-commerce accelerated meaningfully, boosting our mix.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to provide more detail on our financial results.

Maria Gonzalez (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q2. Net sales were $3.15 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.5%, impacted by elevated commodity costs like cocoa and dairy but offset by productivity gains and pricing actions. Operating income was $520 million, and earnings per share were $0.92. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

To give you more color on the six key areas Alex highlighted, let me dive in starting with the performance of our key brands and product categories, which underpinned these Q2 results and continue to demonstrate the resilience of our portfolio amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment. NutriCorp Holdings operates across four core pillars: Beverages, Snacks & Confectionery, Dairy & Plant-Based Alternatives, and Health & Wellness Nutritionals. We reported aggregate category net revenue growth of 7.2% year-over-year, with organic growth—excluding FX and M&A—at 6.1%. This was fueled by a mix of volume expansion in high-margin segments, disciplined pricing actions averaging 4.5% globally, and market share gains totaling 110 basis points per Nielsen and IRI syndicated data.

Starting with Beverages, which accounted for 38% of our divisional revenue and grew 4.8% organically. Our flagship carbonated soft drinks portfolio, led by the iconic Sparkle Cola brand, delivered 3.2% volume growth in North America, where we expanded all-commodity volume distribution to 92% in convenience channels, up from 89% last year. Pricing was up 5.1% to offset input cost inflation from aluminum and HFCS, which peaked at 12% YoY earlier this year but has moderated to 7%. A bright spot was our zero-sugar variants, which surged 15% in volume, capturing share from legacy players amid the low-cal trend. In Europe, regulatory headwinds around HFSS taxes in the UK and France tempered growth to 2.1%, but our hydration sub-category—anchored by PureSpring bottled water—posted double-digit gains of 11.4%, driven by premium alkaline and flavored extensions. APAC was the star, with 9.7% organic growth, led by energy drinks under the SurgeMax brand, which gained 220 bps share in China’s convenience store channel per Kantar data, benefiting from urbanization and an 18% rise in out-of-home consumption post-COVID mobility recovery. Strategically, we're accelerating our "Beyond Sugar" initiative, investing $150 million in R&D for functional beverages with adaptogens and electrolytes, targeting a $25 billion TAM by 2027.

Turning to Snacks & Confectionery, our largest segment at 42% of revenue, which grew 9.1% organically—well ahead of the global savory snacks category's 5.2% IRI-tracked growth. Crunchy Bites, our kettle chip franchise, was the powerhouse, up 12.3% in revenue with 7.8% volume uplift, powered by the launch of air-fried, 40% less oil variants that resonated with health-conscious Gen Z consumers. In North America, velocity—units per store per week—jumped 14% in club channels like Costco and Sam's, where we hit 98% ACV. Pricing discipline at 4.8% helped margins expand 210 bps to 32.4%.

Confectionery faced pockets of pressure from cocoa inflation, which spiked 45% YoY, capping growth at 5.6%. However, our chocolate-coated nut extensions under NutriJoy gained traction in LATAM, up 18% amid Brazil's premiumization wave, where consumers traded up 22% per Nielsen Homescan. Regionally, Europe delivered 8.2% growth despite soft demand in Germany from economic slowdown, offset by strong club store performance in Spain. Our technical playbook here includes precision fermentation pilots for cocoa alternatives, partnering with DSM to derisk supply chains, and AI-optimized flavor profiling that's reduced time-to-market by 30%. Looking ahead, we're pruning low-velocity SKUs—10% of the portfolio—to fuel innovation in protein-fortified snacks, eyeing a 15% category CAGR through 2028.

Dairy & Plant-Based Alternatives rounded out at 12% of revenue, surging 11.7% organically as plant-based continues its structural shift. Dairy staples like our Heritage Cheese block grew steadily at 6.2%, buoyed by 3.5% pricing to combat milk powder inflation, now easing to 8% YoY. But the real momentum is in alt-dairy: Oat Bliss oat milk jumped 22% in volume, stealing 150 bps from almond leaders in the US refrigerated set, per IRI. North America led with 14.5% growth, driven by e-commerce penetration hitting 28% of sales via Amazon and Instacart partnerships.

In Europe, where plant-based penetration is 12% versus 8% globally, we expanded to 15.3% growth, with barista blends gaining in coffee chains like Starbucks EU. APAC lagged at 7.1% due to rice milk preferences in Southeast Asia, but we're countering with localized coconut variants. Margins here expanded 180 bps to 28.7% via vertical integration—our new US pea protein facility is 40% complete, targeting $50/ton cost savings. Strategically, this category embodies our "Flexitarian Future" thesis: blending dairy mastery with alt-proteins to capture the $40 billion global opportunity, with 25 new SKUs slated for H2.

Finally, Health & Wellness Nutritionals, our fastest grower at 8% of revenue and 14.2% organic expansion, outpacing the $100 billion category's 10% IRI pace. ProFuel protein bars rocketed 19% on 12% volume, with high-protein (20g+) SKUs driving 65% of incremental sales. North America velocity soared 25% in mass channels, while Europe benefited from clean-label certifications amid EU Green Deal regs.

Regionally, LATAM exploded 21% with vitamin-fortified snacks tailored to micronutrient gaps in Mexico and Colombia. Challenges persist in price-sensitive emerging markets, but our DTC platform—now 15% of segment sales—delivers 45% gross margins via subscription models. Initiatives include blockchain traceability for organic claims, boosting consumer trust scores by 18 points per YouGov polls, and co-creation with influencers for 30 viral TikTok launches.

In summary there, our brands are thriving through premiumization—up 16% in mix shift—channel shifts to e-comm and club (now 22% of sales), and sustainability creds like 25% recycled packaging across beverages. Market share expanded in 9 of 10 tracked categories, per Circana data. Risks include persistent inflation in commodities like sugar (+9%) and labor, but our $2.2 billion productivity program—AI demand forecasting, zero-based budgeting—offsets this, delivering 300 bps margin accretion YTD. We're confident in our FY guidance: 6-8% organic growth, with Nutritionals and Snacks leading.

Next, on overall company performance highlights, we had a standout quarter amid the challenging backdrop. Our team delivered resilient top- and bottom-line results, driven by disciplined pricing execution, robust volume growth in high-margin categories, and the early payoffs from our 'Taste the Future' strategic transformation agenda. Consolidated net revenues reached $3.15 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year, or 6.1% on an organic basis excluding FX and minor M&A. This marks our sixth straight quarter of organic growth, outpacing the broader CPG industry average. Volume/mix contributed 2.1 percentage points—led by double-digit gains in plant-based and functional beverages—while pricing added 4 points to offset input cost inflation in cocoa, dairy, and edible oils, which remain elevated but have eased sequentially.

Gross profit expanded to lift adjusted gross margin to 38.5%, a 150 basis point improvement, fueled by supply chain efficiencies like a 10% reduction in logistics costs and favorable hedging—we locked in 70% of 2024 cocoa needs at levels 18% below current futures. Adjusted operating income rose to $520 million, margins at 16.5%, EBITDA at 20.8%. Diluted adjusted EPS at $0.92, benefiting from $150 million in share repurchases.

By segments, Beverages at 42% posted strong organic growth with volumes outpacing peers, thanks to club channel velocity and zero-sugar rollouts. Snacks & Confectionery delivered solid gains, with premium salty snacks up double-digits on e-commerce and SKU rationalization pruning 12% of low-velocity items. Convenience Foods grew steadily with pricing offsetting protein inflation.

Regionally, North America led with market share gains to 14.2% in non-alcoholic beverages per Circana, and foodservice recovery up 18%. EMEA advanced despite sentiment softness, with functional yogurt share gains. Emerging markets achieved double-digit growth, led by APAC juices and LATAM inflation pass-through. FX shaved 40 bps off top line.

Underpinning this are AI-powered demand sensing across 85% of SKUs, reducing forecast error by 28%, sustainability scaling to 40% of cocoa regen-ag, DTC e-commerce at 18% of NA sales with 22% repeat rates, premiumization in 65% of innovation, and strong cash flow funding capex. In summary, this positions us to raise full-year outlooks while navigating inflation and shifts to healthier options.

Moving to e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, this continues to be a cornerstone of our omnichannel strategy. In Q2, e-commerce sales reached $478 million, up 48% year-over-year and now 15.2% of our total net revenue—up from 10.1% last year. This marks accelerating double-digit growth, capitalizing on consumers' shift to convenience and personalization amid grocery inflation.

DTC via NutriFresh Direct drove 62% at $296 million, up 55%, with AOV at $68 on subscriptions from 1.2 million members at 78% retention, yielding 32% gross margins. Marketplace like Amazon Fresh and Instacart took 38%, up 38%, with plant-based snacks up 62% in units and RTD beverages capturing 18% share in the $12 billion US market.

North America at 72% grew 52% from millennials/Gen Z. Europe up 42% via Ocado and Rewe. APAC 28% with quick-commerce in India. Initiatives include AI personalization lifting conversions 34%, CAC down 18% to $14, LTV at $312, micro-fulfillment cutting delivery to under 2 hours, spoilage under 1%. E-commerce data informs launches like ProteinPulse shakes, with 8-point margin premium. We expect 40-45% growth in H2, to 14.5% full-year contribution.

On the impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, it's been a notable headwind with over 55% of revenue from international markets. Reported net revenues grew 4.2% to $3.15 billion, but organic constant-currency was 7.1%, with adverse FX a $285 million headwind or 230 bps drag—the third straight quarter, totaling $750 million YTD.

Regionally, Europe (28% international) saw Euro down 8%, shaving $112 million from hydration brands; Pound down 5% hit UK snacks $22 million. LATAM (22%) Brazilian Real down 12% $95 million on sodas despite 9% volumes; Mexico Peso 4% $28 million. APAC (18%) Yen down 15% $68 million on RTD coffee; China stable but EM currencies added $42 million drag.

Hedging covered 75% of exposures at favorable rates, protecting $180 million; natural hedges from 65% local COGS sourcing. Initiatives: localizing production in Mexico cutting imports 25%, AI dynamic pricing for 2-3 extra points, currency swaps in Turkey. Q3 headwind 100-150 bps expected; diversified portfolio limits volatility.

Regarding revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, we're pleased to reaffirm with slight refinement reflecting healthier platforms momentum, offset by commodities. Consolidated net sales $12.4-12.6 billion, 4-6% reported, 5-7% organic, incorporating 2% FX headwind from stronger USD vs. euro/BRL. Pricing 4-5 points, volume 1-2 points.

Adjusted EPS $3.45-3.60, 6-10% growth, with favorability from debt refinancing $0.05, productivity $0.03, headwind from cocoa +45% YTD and wheat +15% $0.10. Gross margin 38-39%, EBITDA 19.5-20% via $180 million Supply Chain Excellence savings—automated lines, AI inventory. Free cash flow $1.2-1.3 billion supporting $0.85 dividend up 5%, $400 million repurchases; capex $650 million.

North America 6-8% organic on premiumization like low-sugar energy +22%. EMEA 4-6% with plant-based up 18% offsetting soda dips. APAC/LATAM 7-9% on e-comm 18%, Brazil volumes +12%. Embeds 'Health Forward 2026' for $2 billion incremental from reformulations (65% beverages under 5g sugar), sustainability hedging volatility, SAP S/4HANA at 92% forecast accuracy. Risks: $150 million extra inflation, downtrading; upsides M&A, tariff relief. This positions us for mid-single-digit growth, double-digit TSR.

Finally, on organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, for Q3 we guide 4-6%, full-year 5-7%, reflecting consumer momentum tempered by costs. FY24 actual 6.2% with 2.8% volume, 3.4% pricing; Nutrition & Snacks +8.1%.

Segments: Beverages 3-5% Q3 to 5-7% FY, functional like VitaHydrate +25% ahead, RTD coffee double-digits. Nutrition & Snacks 6-8% Q3 to 7-9%, NutriBar penetration +4 points. Convenience 2-4% to 4-6% on keto innovations.

Regions: NA 5-7% on snacks share +80 bps, C-store +15%. Europe 2-4% plant-based +22%. EM 8-10% Brazil/India juices/snacks.

Trends: 2-3% price/mix premiumization, 2-4% volume innovation. Initiatives: 70% localized sourcing, e-comm +28% velocity, 40% regen-ag launches, post-divestiture BFY at 55%. EPS $4.85-5.05, FCF $1.2B. Risks inflation/weak volumes, upsides RTD/APAC.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales $12.4-12.6 billion, organic 5-7%, EPS $3.45-3.60.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
If you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Johnson (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Good morning, Mike. Inflation remains a challenge, particularly in commodities like cocoa up 45% and dairy up 12%, but we've executed disciplined pricing averaging 4.5% globally, which consumers have accepted well without meaningful volume erosion. Our $2.2 billion productivity program, including AI forecasting and supply chain optimizations, has delivered 300 bps margin accretion YTD, more than offsetting these pressures. We're hedged on 70% of key inputs and focused on premiumization to protect margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Sarah Lee (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for VitaHydrate and what is the expected impact of the product?

Tom Ellis (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Sarah. VitaHydrate, our new zero-sugar electrolyte line, is off to a strong start post-Q2 launch, tracking 25% ahead of forecasts and gaining 150 bps share in the functional beverage space against Gatorade and Powerade per Nielsen. Plans include national rollout to 85% ACV by year-end, with H2 marketing spend up 20% focused on Gen Z via TikTok and athlete endorsements. We expect it to contribute $200 million in incremental revenue FY25, driving 2 points to overall organic growth and expanding category margins through 20g protein variants.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

David Kim (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Lisa Chen (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. We've built resilience through diversification—now 70% localized sourcing for wheat and proteins, reducing FX exposure 40%—and AI-driven forecasting via SAP IBP cutting inventory days to 45 and stockouts 25%. Micro-fulfillment centers and carrier consolidation lowered logistics 10%, while regen-ag partnerships cover 40% cocoa/palm to mitigate weather risks like Panama Canal issues. Our new pea protein facility and hedging de-risk cocoa at 60%, keeping service levels at 98%.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Chen with Citi. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Citi):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Maria Gonzalez (CFO):
Thanks, Emily. We're reaffirming full-year guidance with conviction: 5-7% organic sales, EPS $3.45-3.60, FCF $1.2-1.3B. Q3 organic 4-6%, accelerating H2 on innovation ramps like functional beverages and e-comm scaling to 40% growth. Pricing power, premium mix shift +16%, and productivity sustain margins at 38-39%. EM growth 7-9% offsets any NA softness; FX 1-1.5% headwind assumed. Overall, positioned for sustained momentum.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCorp Holdings. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
